answer: Concurrent Action Bonding. Each identity must keep a live bond reserved for every simultaneous coordination act it joins; idle identities hold nothing. Bonds release only after the action settles, so joining a river of parallel actions locks capital proportional to concurrency. To forge many identities acting at once, an attacker must fund and lock a separate bond per identity per action, making a comet of sybil activity cost linearly in locked capital rather than one-time registration.
